subject: Initial request: SOC 2 Type II report access, priority artifacts, and bridge letter options
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: security@acme-corp.com, audits@acme-corp.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial request: SOC 2 Type II report access, priority artifacts, and bridge letter options

Hi Acme security team,

Hope you’re well. We’re kicking off our security & procurement checklist for Redwood Inference (vendor intake ID ACME-2026-REDW-01) and need the following items to complete a light review and to satisfy our compliance gating for a production connection: 

Priority requested items (minimal ask to progress):
- SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) covering controls for the period that most closely aligns with May 1, 2025 — Apr 30, 2026. If you have multiple reports, the most recent Type II is preferred.
- If the report period does not cover our desired window, a signed bridge letter describing the effective coverage dates and any interim control changes.
- Control descriptions or system boundary statement (short doc or spreadsheet).
- Retention policy summary and sample log retention configuration (one-page).
- If available: CAIQ or SIG Lite export (JSON/CSV/PDF).

File transfer options we can accept: pre-signed S3 link (preferred), secure ShareFile link, or an encrypted email attachment. We can also accept an upload to our intake folder if you’d like a pre-signed link from us.

Recommendations and quick asks: please flag any redactions in the PDF (PII, IP) and confirm whether the auditor who issued the report is a licensed CPA firm.

Would it be possible to share the items above by EOD Friday, Jul 3? If that timeline does not work, please propose the earliest available date and whether a bridge letter is possible for the exact audit window we requested.

Thanks — below are a couple of short reply templates you can use if helpful (I’ll also share internal snippets shortly):

Quick confirm (external): 
"We can share the SOC 2 Type II report and bridge letter via pre-signed S3 by Jul 3. Attachments: Acme_Soc2_TypeII_202504.pdf, Acme_SOC2_Bridge_Letter_Jun2026.pdf"

Quick decline/propose new date: 
"We can provide the Type II report on Jul 10 and will include a bridge letter covering May 2025–Apr 2026. Would that timeline work?"

Appreciate the help — cc’ing Kim and Ben for intake/verification.

Best,
Olga
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: evidence_manifest_template.xlsx (we can send this if helpful)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial request: SOC 2 Type II report access, priority artifacts, and bridge letter options

On Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 09:12 AM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Acme security team,
> 
> Hope you’re well. We’re kicking off our security & procurement checklist...

Thanks, Olga — echoing this. A couple of internal notes and suggested concise replies for Acme so they can hit a timeline quickly: 

Priority guidance for internal reviewers (Ben + Olga):
- Confirm the scope: whether the SOC report includes our expected product lines (infrastructure layer vs. managed product). If ambiguous ask for the system boundary statement.
- Verify auditor firm name is on the cover page and that it's a CPA firm.
- Bridge letter: if the report ends before Apr 30, 2026 we accept a dated bridge letter that states the controls remained in place and references the auditor/firm if possible.

Suggested one-line templates to paste into Acme reply: 
1) Fast share: "We can provide the SOC 2 Type II PDF and bridge letter via pre-signed S3 link by Jul 2; will include control descriptions and retention policy summary."
2) Slight delay: "We will share the report on Jul 10; bridge letter will be provided and the auditor details will be included in the cover section."

Transfer preferences: pre-signed S3 is easiest for us. If they prefer, we can create the pre-signed bucket and share upload instructions (let me know).

I'll draft a short intake email we can send if they reply with attachments.

-Kim

---
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Enablement (Security)
Redwood Inference
From: Acme Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: audits@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 08:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial request: SOC 2 Type II report access, priority artifacts, and bridge letter options

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the checklist and timeline. We can share the requested artifacts. Please note: our most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers the period 2024-05-01 through 2025-04-30. We can provide a signed bridge letter that confirms coverage and that there were no control exceptions relevant to the areas you flagged during the subsequent period through Apr 30, 2026.

Planned share:
- Acme_SOC2_TypeII_202504_Report.pdf (attached)
- Acme_SOC2_Bridge_Letter_Jun2026.pdf (attached)
- Control boundary statement (PDF)
- Log retention summary (one-page PDF)
- CAIQ-lite export (CSV) — note this is an exported template with some fields redacted for confidentiality

Transfer: We will upload the package to a pre-signed S3 link you provide, or we can send via our secure ShareFile if you prefer.

Please confirm whether you want us to redact auditor internal notes (we will leave auditor firm and report dates visible).

Best,
J. Morales
Security Operations Manager
Acme Corp

Thanks — this works well.

Quick confirmations:
- Pre-signed S3 upload preferred. We’ll create a short-lived bucket and share the presigned URL by EOD today.
- Please leave auditor firm name and report dates visible; redacting internal auditor notes is fine.
- We’ll prioritize the PDF and the bridge letter when triaging.

Next steps for Redwood: Ben will verify the PDF once uploaded and confirm acceptance of redactions. Kim will log the report in HubSpot and attach the link to deal ACME-2026-REDW-01.

Thanks again — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Olga
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
